hook: SCP-5655 is an empty Spam can that releases a 7.5cm translucent red genie when you shake it. That sounds like the start of a cautionary tale about careless wishing, but the test log heads somewhere gentler. Take the wishes one at a time rather than skimming: the gap between what is asked and what arrives is where the jokes live, and the genie's personality slowly shows through its results.
whyItMatters: It is a Safe-class reality bender whose power is small, earnest and almost always a little off target. The article spends most of its length on a run of underwhelming results that look like plain failure, and then a single incident log at the end recasts all of them. What lingers afterward is less fear than a mild, oddly kind sense of humor.
thingsToNotice: An orange ball arrives as a tangerine with a bite missing, at the same moment part of Junior Researcher Dinns's lunch vanishes; a heavy stone lands on the genie itself; asked for something strong, it lifts that stone and points at its own chest. The million dollars turns out to be Liberian dollars, roughly 6,200 USD per the footnote, the wish to raise the dead yields ska tracks credited to Gene E, and two requests for the key to happiness produce a used Kerplunk and then, after three months of reading philosophy, an unopened one. Only when Alami asks it to balance the Foundation's budget does it speak, explaining that her reality is so fragile that every wish is like pulling a Jenga block, so it has been holding back all along. It cites a clause from an interuniversal handbook to refuse, admits it cannot rewrite those rules, and offers her a coffee instead. The coffee is cold, and it confesses it added enough sugar that she would not notice.
